source_name: Clarity Project — company/tender dossier (EDRPOU-keyed)
why_relevant: Aggregates registry, tax, litigation and full tender history per EDRPOU, both as buyer and as bidder. Fast way to snowball from a known NBU-family entity to its suppliers and to related legal entities.

source_name: YouControl — company profile, PrJSC Ukrainian Processing Centre (EDRPOU 24747867)
why_relevant: UPC is the largest independent processor and an early PROSTIR participant, but is a private JSC and therefore not a Prozorro buyer. Registry aggregators are the practical route to its ownership, financials and counterparty links.

source_name: Opendatabot — EDRPOU-keyed registry monitoring with API and change alerts
why_relevant: Provides push alerts on registry changes (directors, capital, status, court cases, tender activity) for named entities — an efficient watchdog layer over the NBU-family and processor entity list.

source_name: NBU — payment systems register and PROSTIR section (bank.gov.ua/payments)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map for this cell: registers of payment systems, PROSTIR/NPSMU participants, processing centres (incl. PrJSC UPC) and SEP participants. Snowballing this list produces the buyer/vendor universe to monitor in Prozorro.

source_name: PROSTIR national card system official site (prostir.gov.ua)
why_relevant: Scheme-level publisher for the national card system: participant lists, technical/certification requirements and modernisation announcements that precede or accompany procurement of processing and card-issuing technology.

source_name: Infobox Prozorro — NBU procurement practice guidance and case articles
why_relevant: Prozorro's own editorial channel published NBU-specific procurement practice notes, revealing how the central bank structures its tenders (procedure types, exemptions, wartime practice) — essential for building correct collection filters.

source_name: CS Ltd (ЦС Лтд) press centre — SEP 4.1 / instant payments implementation communications
why_relevant: Vendor-side disclosure: core-banking supplier publicising its SEP 4.1 instant-payments implementation. Vendor press rooms reveal which suppliers actually win and deliver NBU rail-adjacent work, often before or instead of contract-level disclosure.

source_name: Ukrainian financial trade press (Minfin, Mind.ua, FinClub, RBC-Ukraine) — SEP/instant-payments rollout reporting
why_relevant: Reports NBU rail roadmaps (SEP-4 on ISO 20022, instant credit transfers from Dec 2024, 2025-2030 modernisation roadmap, multicurrency/cross-border) with dates and bank counts — the demand signal that precedes and explains tender waves.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine — Procurement page (Закупівлі у Райффайзен Банку)
why_relevant: Official procurement landing page of the largest foreign-owned bank in Ukraine. States procurement principles, names the e-procurement stack (Oracle iProcurement), links a supplier self-registration MS Forms questionnaire, publishes dated standard contractual terms (editions 18.04.2024 and 29.04.2025), and names a Procurement Category Manager with direct email/phone. Gives both the onboarding route and a versioned document trail to monitor.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Aval — commercial tenders on E-Tender (biz.e-tender.ua)
why_relevant: Raiffeisen publicly selected E-Tender as its supplier-sourcing marketplace; actual price-request procedures (e.g. CCTV software, equipment maintenance) are announced there. This is the closest thing to a Prozorro-style feed for a bank that is outside public procurement law, so it exposes real demand categories, timing and sometimes counterparties.

source_name: Zakupivli.Pro — commercial tenders of AT Raiffeisen Bank Aval (EDRPOU 14305909)
why_relevant: Second marketplace carrying the same issuer's commercial procurements, queryable by EDRPOU code. EDRPOU-scoped querying is the key trick: it lets the same collector be pointed at any private bank without depending on the bank publishing anything itself.

source_name: Zakupivli.Pro — commercial procurements of PAT PUMB (EDRPOU 14282829)
why_relevant: PUMB does not appear to publish a procurement/supplier section on its own site, so this aggregator page is currently the only observed public window onto PUMB's commercial buying. High value precisely because the direct channel is absent.

source_name: OTP Bank Ukraine — Tender regulations (Положення «Про проведення тендерів в АТ ОТП Банк»)
why_relevant: Full published internal tender rulebook: equal treatment of domestic/foreign bidders, mandatory counterparty reputation pre-check, one proposal per bidder, 15-30 day announcement windows, sealed-envelope submission, 15-day evaluation protocol, 14-day contract signature. This is a rare case of a private bank exposing its procurement procedure in detail — directly usable for bid-preparation and cycle-time modelling.

source_name: OTP Bank Ukraine — list of active tenders
why_relevant: Live, dated tender announcements with subject, window and sometimes the winning supplier (e.g. a translation-services tender won by 'ГРУПА КОМПАНІЙ ФОРС'). Winner disclosure on a private bank site is unusual and makes this a genuine award-notice source, not just an RFP board.

source_name: APS-TENDER — OTP Bank issuer instance (otpbank.aps-tender.com)
why_relevant: OTP Bank states all its tenders run through the APS-TENDER e-marketplace; each announcement links into a bank-branded instance. Holds the actual tender documentation, requirements and bidding mechanics behind the public headline.

source_name: Credit Agricole Bank Ukraine — Закупівлі (procurement & supplier onboarding)
why_relevant: Fully articulated three-step vendor onboarding: online supplier questionnaire, capability presentation to a dedicated Vendors@ mailbox, then invitation to competitive bidding via a mandatory anketa. Also publishes a procurement-process roadmap PDF, dated mandatory contract clauses (13.06.2024 and 06.05.2020) and an explicit anti-corruption supplier conduct standard with a group whistleblowing channel.

source_name: UkrSibbank (BNP Paribas Group) — Закупівлі / supplier expression-of-interest form
why_relevant: UkrSibbank runs a closed-invitation model: no public tender board, instead a standing supplier interest form (company, goods/services offered, sector, track record) from which the bank issues invitations to competitive procurement. The page also carries a Suppliers' CSR Charter in UA and EN — the vendor code-of-conduct artefact for the BNP-owned bank.

source_name: BNP Paribas Group — Suppliers page & Sustainable Procurement / CSR Charter
why_relevant: Parent-level procurement doctrine that cascades to UkrSibbank. Explicitly states BNP Paribas does not practise open bidding — a supplier either lands on a preferred-supplier list after a call for tenders or is selected for a specific project — and that vendors are pre-qualified on financial soundness and economic dependence. Group tooling is named (OneProcTool / Ivalua, DocuSign). This explains why UA-level visibility is so thin and where the real gate sits.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International — Group Supplier Code of Conduct (PDF, 08/2025)
why_relevant: Binding contractual annex for anyone supplying any RBI Group entity, including Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine. Sets COP21 climate alignment, human-rights and fair-competition obligations, and forbids sharing RBI procurement information with third parties — the last clause directly constrains what suppliers and therefore intelligence collection can expect to see. Dated version (08/2025) makes it trackable.

source_name: OTP Group — ESG guidelines in procurement (PDF) & Partner Code of Ethics
why_relevant: OTP Group's procurement-facing ESG rulebook plus a separate Partner Code of Ethics setting minimum standards for suppliers, sponsored partners and other counterparties across group members, including OTP Bank Ukraine. Defines the qualification bar a vendor must clear before OTP Ukraine's tender process even starts.

source_name: Credit Agricole Group — ethics alert / whistleblowing platform (BKMS)
why_relevant: Named by Credit Agricole Bank Ukraine as the channel for reporting supplier-side corruption, collusion and conflicts of interest, in 11 languages including Ukrainian. Confirms the enforcement layer behind the bank's supplier conduct rules; useful for assessing how tightly vendor behaviour is policed rather than for content collection.

source_name: KredoBank (PKO BP Group) — Тендери та закупівлі
why_relevant: Foreign-owned (Polish PKO BP) private bank not in the original cell list but structurally identical to it. Runs all procurement through SmartTender.biz under an internal Положення про закупівлі, distinguishes open/closed tenders and simplified procedures, publishes a Code of Ethics for tender participants, and exposes a live open-tender mirror link. A clean template for how a foreign-parent bank in UA externalises its tendering.

source_name: SmartTender.biz — commercial e-trading platform (bank issuer tenants)
why_relevant: One of the three marketplaces private UA banks route commercial procurement through (confirmed for KredoBank; Credit Agricole documents also surface here). Free supplier registration. As a pointer it lets you enumerate which financial institutions are issuing commercial tenders at all — a discovery surface for banks that never announce on their own sites.

source_name: Zakupivli.Pro — commercial procurement platform (issuer directory)
why_relevant: Prozorro-accredited marketplace that also hosts privately-issued commercial procurement, searchable by buyer EDRPOU. Its own blog documents multi-year commercial-procurement relationships with banks (e.g. Piraeus Bank MKB), naming actors that never surface on bank websites. The single best enumeration surface for the cell.
